title: The little sign that conquered the world
text: The @ sign had spent centuries {{1}} accounting, {{2}} it simply meant 'at the price of', before {{3}} was drafted for an entirely new job. {{4}} was Ray Tomlinson, {{5}} needed a way to separate a person's name {{6}} their computer on the early internet, and he chose the @ sign for the task in 1971. The sign then travelled {{7}} email went, and each language gave it a nickname of its own: ape tail, little duck, strudel. Today it fronts social media handles and art exhibitions, and a symbol invented for sacks of wheat now sits {{8}} the centre of how humanity addresses itself.

gaps.explanation: 'Where' refers back to accounting as the setting.
'It' refers to the sign as the subject.

gaps.hint: cleft pronoun: ___ was Ray Tomlinson who
gaps.explanation: The cleft sentence emphasises the person.
Non-defining relative about a person after the comma.

gaps.hint: preposition: separate a name ___ their computer
gaps.explanation: 'Separate X from Y' — the fixed verb pattern.
'Wherever' — to every place that email reached.
'At the centre of' is the fixed phrase.
